blocks.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Fa provider for run-agent.sh
#
# fa headless contract (env preconfig — the declaration is machine-written
# and self-contained; fa never guesses catalog defaults):
#   FA_PROVIDER_TYPE     (required) catalog provider kind: anthropic,
#                        google, dial, openai-completions, zai, aiin,
#                        minimax, chatgpt-codex, copilot, codemie,
#                        ollama, openai, openrouter, kimi, …
#   FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG   (required, JSON) {"baseUrl": …, "model": …,
#                        "apiKeyEnvVar": …} — baseUrl and model are
#                        mandatory (fa fails the boot without them),
#                        apiKeyEnvVar names the env var that carries the
#                        API key (its _BASE64 twin also accepted)
#   FA_PROVIDER_NAME     (optional) unique entry name override
#   FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY  (optional) convenience: mapped into the env var
#                        the config's apiKeyEnvVar names — ONLY inside
#                        the fa subprocess scope
#
# Sessions (when agents/setup/fa-session.sh is present, e.g. AI Teammate
# runs): --session "$FA_SESSION_NAME" --session-root "$FA_SESSION_ROOT"
# resume-or-create the deterministic named session for repo:ticket:group.

_fa_resolve_env() {
  if [ -z "${FA_PROVIDER_TYPE:-}" ]; then
    echo "Error: FA_PROVIDER_TYPE environment variable is required for fa provider" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  if [ -z "${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG:-}" ]; then
    echo "Error: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is required for fa provider — a JSON object with at least {\"baseUrl\", \"model\"} (fa never guesses catalog defaults), e.g." >&2
    echo "  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{\"baseUrl\":\"https://ai-proxy.lab.epam.com\",\"model\":\"gpt-4o\",\"apiKeyEnvVar\":\"DIAL_API_KEY\"}'" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  # Surface the config's key env var name so the runner can map
  # FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY into it for the subprocess when the var itself
  # is unset.
  FA_KEY_ENV_VAR="$(printf '%s' "${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG}" | sed -n 's/.*"apiKeyEnvVar"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
}

run_fa() {
  _fa_resolve_env || return 1

  _fa_configure_session

  echo "Fa Configuration:"
  echo "  Provider Type: ${FA_PROVIDER_TYPE}"
  [ -n "${FA_PROVIDER_NAME:-}" ] && echo "  Entry Name: ${FA_PROVIDER_NAME}"
  echo "  Config: ${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG}"

  local pass_args=()
  local arg
  for arg in ${PASS_ARGS[@]+"${PASS_ARGS[@]}"}; do
    case "$arg" in
      --continue|--resume) ;;
      *) pass_args+=("$arg") ;;
    esac
  done

  # Provider selection is driven entirely by the FA_PROVIDER_* env
  # preconfig (fa precedence: explicit flags > preconfig > saved config).
  # No --provider/--model/--base-url flags here — the env declaration is
  # the single source of truth and pins every model role.
  local cmd
  cmd=(fa)
  if [ -n "${FA_SESSION_NAME:-}" ] && [ -n "${FA_SESSION_ROOT:-}" ]; then
    cmd+=(--session "${FA_SESSION_NAME}" --session-root "${FA_SESSION_ROOT}")
  fi
  # FA_LOG_FILE (optional): tee fa's full stdout trace (assistant text, tool
  # calls) to this file — untruncated, unlike the terminal-width trajectory
  # rows. CI tails/uploads it; requires fa >= v0.1.335 (--log-file).
  # Callers can still pass --log-file explicitly via PASS_ARGS.
  if [ -n "${FA_LOG_FILE:-}" ] \
    && ! printf '%s\n' ${pass_args[@]+"${pass_args[@]}"} | grep -qx -- '--log-file'; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "${FA_LOG_FILE}")"
    cmd+=(--log-file "${FA_LOG_FILE}")
  fi
  cmd+=(${pass_args[@]+"${pass_args[@]}"} -p "$PROMPT")

  echo "Working directory: $(pwd)"
  echo ""
  echo "Running: ${cmd[*]}"
  echo ""

  local agent_log
  agent_log="$(mktemp)"

  # Map FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY into the env var the config's apiKeyEnvVar
  # names — ONLY for the fa subprocess (claude.sh maps CLAUDE_CODE_* →
  # ANTHROPIC_* the same way) so it never leaks into the surrounding job
  # environment. When the caller already exported the named var, fa reads
  # it directly and nothing is injected.
  set +e
  if [ -n "${FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY:-}" ] && [ -n "${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR:-}" ] \
     && [ -z "$(eval "echo \${${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR}:-}")" ]; then
    env "${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR}=${FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY}" "${cmd[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$agent_log"
  else
    "${cmd[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$agent_log"
  fi
  local exit_code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
  set -e

  record_codegraph_usage "$agent_log"
  rm -f "$agent_log"

  echo ""
  echo "=== Agent completed with exit code: $exit_code ==="
  return $exit_code
}

# Configure the deterministic session when the setup script is available
# (repo-local runs may not have it — fa then runs without a named session).
# Runs inside run_fa's caller context, NOT at source time: sourcing here
# would otherwise run before the provider env validation and leak setup
# vars into unrelated shells.
_fa_configure_session() {
  local setup_dir
  setup_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../setup" 2>/dev/null && pwd || true)"
  if [ -z "${FA_SESSION_NAME:-}" ] && [ -f "${setup_dir}/fa-session.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source "${setup_dir}/fa-session.sh" env
  fi
}

So the fa provider is invoked via `bash agents/scripts/run-agent.sh --continue <promptPath>`. Note that `run_fa` ignores `--continue|--resume` in PASS_ARGS but `FA_SESSION_NAME`/`FA_SESSION_ROOT` make it use `--session "$FA_SESSION_NAME" --session-root "$FA_SESSION_ROOT"` which is a "resume-or-create the deterministic named session". So a plain re-invocation of `run-agent.sh` with the fa provider already resumes the persisted session (resume-or-create). That means the "bounded resume" mechanism (feedbackLoop.resumeAgent with `--continue`) works for the fa provider as "resume the same session".

The ticket says: "It runs the same fa `--session` (the session is still on the runner) after a backoff (default 90s, `customParams.providerTransientBackoffSec`). At most one resume per leg."

So the implementation plan:

1. **quotaCircuitBreaker.classifyFailure** gains kind `provider_transient`:
  - Matches `Provider chain exhausted` together with only 5xx / 429 / network attempts (no 401/403/quota text).
  - quota_exhausted keeps priority (I1).
  - The classification should also extract the model list and codes for the comment (AC5: comment names the provider + codes).

2. **developTicketAndCreatePR.recoverMissingResponse**:
  - After quotaParkGate and fatal check, classify the interrupted text.
  - If classification is `provider_transient` → perform the bounded resume even when the generic resume flag is off (i.e. force-enable `feedbackLoop.missingResponse.enabled`), with a backoff before the resume (default 90s, `customParams.providerTransientBackoffSec`).
  - At most one resume per leg — the missingResponse stage marker `missing_response` already enforces maxAttempts=1. But wait — I2 says "never more than one resume per leg". The existing `resumeOnceForMissingResponse` uses marker `outputs/feedback/<ticketKey>_missing_response.atempt`. Since the leg is one run, this marker file persists on disk across the two calls in the same leg (noChangesResponse + ensureResponseForPrBody both call recoverMissingResponse). Hmm — within one leg, both call sites could attempt a resume. With maxAttempts=1 forced, the second call would be blocked by the attempt marker (attempt >= maxAttempts). Good — that enforces I2 within the leg as long as the marker file persists.

  Actually wait — if the resume "lands response.md", the first site returns content and no second call happens. If resume doesn't land, first site returns null → reset path → throws. So only one call site fires per leg typically.

  For the forced provider-transient resume: I need to pass an override so `resumeOnceForMissingResponse` doesn't bail on `!isFeedbackEnabled`. Options:
  - Add a new option to `resumeOnceForMissingResponse`: `force: true` (or `forceEnabled: true`) which skips the enablement gate. This keeps one implementation.
  - In developTicketAndCreatePR, when classification is provider_transient, call `feedbackLoop.resumeOnceForMissingResponse({ ticketKey, customParams, force: true, backoffSeconds })`.

  And the backoff: "runs ... after a backoff (default 90s, `customParams.providerTransientBackoffSec`)". Backoff must be honored and testable (AC6, fake timer/sleep injection). The resume itself is executed by feedbackLoop.resumeAgent via cli_execute_command. The sleep injection: simplest is a `sleepBackoff(seconds)` function in feedbackLoop (or developTicketAndCreatePR) that runs `sleep <n>` via runCommand — in tests we mock `cli_execute_command`. Let me add to feedbackLoop a function `providerTransientResume(options)` that:
  - computes backoff from customParams.providerTransientBackoffSec (default 90)
  - sleeps (runCommand 'sleep N' — blocked from Node? GralJS uses cli_execute_command; in unit tests mocked)
  - calls resumeOnceForMissingResponse with force enabled.

  Hmm, but where to put the backoff logic? AC6 says "the backoff is configurable and honored (UT-5, fake timer/sleep injection)". Testable design: a pure helper `providerTransientBackoffSeconds(customParams)` returning parsed seconds (default 90), and the actual sleep via an injectable function. In feedbackLoop.js, `runCommand` is module-level using cli_execute_command global — tests already mock cli_execute_command (test_feedbackLoop mocks it). Let me check test_feedbackLoop for how they mock sleep-ish behavior.

3. **Reset comment honesty** (AC5): when the leg is reset after a provider-outage (5xx), the comment must say `⏸️ Provider outage (<model list>, <codes>) — reset for retry` rather than "likely hit a rate limit". Currently `interruptedNoChangesComment` says "likely hit a rate limit". Need a classification-aware comment: if the classification is provider_transient with providers/codes, use the honest wording. Otherwise keep the existing text (backwards compat for tests).

4. **Run conclusion**: stays failure on reset (already the case — throwInterruptedReset), success if resume lands response.md (already the case — normal path).

Let me now check `throwInterruptedReset` and the two comment functions' usage. Also need to see how `resetInterruptedDevelopment` is called with `interruptedNoChangesComment(ctx.ticketKey)` — the comment functions need ctx (classification). I'll add a classification-aware comment builder.

Now the classification: current `classifyFailure`:
- quota check first (I1 priority).
- `RATE_LIMIT_RE.test(t) || TIMEOUT_RE.test(t)` → transient.
- else null.

New requirement: kind `provider_transient` when text matches `Provider chain exhausted` AND the failure evidence is only 5xx / 429 / network attempts (no 401/403/quota text).

Question: how does `provider_transient` differ from existing `transient`? The existing `transient` kind covers plain 429/timeout texts without a chain-exhausted tail. The new `provider_transient` is specifically "the whole provider chain failed with transient errors (5xx/429/network)" — chain exhausted tail + only transient attempts. Both are transient in nature; but the dev leg uses `provider_transient` to trigger the resume; plain `transient` keeps... hmm, wait. Should plain `transient` (429 without chain exhausted) also trigger resume? The ticket says: "when the fa CLI exits because the whole provider chain failed with transient errors (5xx / 429), the dev leg is classified provider_transient, resumes ...". So the trigger is the chain-exhausted tail. A plain 429 text without chain exhausted — current classification gives `transient` and the reset path. AC1's fixture: "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2 chain model(s) failed after 6 attempt(s) over 330s" with 500 `{"code":"1234","message":"Internal network failure"}` ×3 and 429 ×12.

Design decision: classifyFailure returns kind `provider_transient` when CHAIN_EXHAUSTED matches and there's transient evidence (5xx/429/network) and NO auth/quota evidence (no 401/403/quota vocabulary). Keep returning `transient` for non-chain texts? Hmm — but then what about a chain-exhausted text with 429s? Currently: RATE_LIMIT_RE matches → transient. So currently chain-exhausted + 429s → `transient` (no park since quotaClassificationOf only parks on quota_exhausted). The new behavior: chain-exhausted + only-5xx/429/network → `provider_transient`.

Should plain `transient` remain for texts without the chain tail? Yes — minimal change: keep `transient` for non-chain transient texts (existing tests), add `provider_transient` for chain-exhausted texts with only transient evidence. This preserves REG tests: "bare Provider chain exhausted without 403/quota evidence → not quota (legacy reset path)" — hmm, this existing test says `assert.notOk(cls && cls.kind === 'quota_exhausted')` — with the change, bare "Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2" would classify as... what? There's no 5xx/429/network evidence. Is bare chain-exhausted `provider_transient`? The ticket: "matches `Provider chain exhausted` together with only 5xx / 429 / network attempts (no 401/403/quota text)". "only 5xx/429/network attempts" — a bare chain-exhausted text has no attempt evidence at all. Strictly "only 5xx/429/network" with zero attempts... ambiguous. I'd say: bare chain-exhausted without any evidence → treat as provider_transient? Or null?

# gh-1121: Dev leg: provider-chain outage (5xx/429) → resume persisted fa session once instead of cold reset; honest cause in comment

## Description

## Goal — a provider outage mid-leg resumes the same session instead of a cold reset (v1)
One sentence: **when the fa CLI exits because the whole provider chain failed with transient errors (5xx / 429), the dev leg is classified `provider_transient`, resumes the persisted fa session once after a backoff, and falls back to the cold reset only if the resume also fails. The ticket comment names the real cause.**

## Live evidence
- Run IstiN/dmtools-agents#39315836954 (job 118277233621), gh-1112, 2026-10-19 20:02–20:14.
- `zai/glm-5.3-flash` returned 500 `{"code":"1234","message":"Internal network failure"}` ×3. `kimi-for-coding` then hit `429 Rate limit reached` ×12, giving `Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2 chain model(s) failed after 6 attempt(s) over 330s`. The agent exited with code 1 after 11 requests and 97k prompt tokens of real work. The session was persisted to `fa-sess/gh-1112`.
- `recoverMissingResponse`:
  - `quotaParkGate`: no (not a quota error, correct).
  - `isFatalCliEnvironmentError`: no.
  - `resumeOnceForMissingResponse` → `Bounded resume … not attempted (disabled)`.
  - Result: cold reset to Ready For Development, a comment saying "likely hit a rate limit", and a red run.
- All of the work is discarded, and the next leg starts from scratch, likely into the same outage.

## Architecture
1. `classifyInterruptedText` / `quotaBreaker.classifyFailure` gains the kind `provider_transient`: matches `Provider chain exhausted` together with only 5xx / 429 / network attempts (no 401/403/quota text).
2. For `provider_transient`, `recoverMissingResponse` performs the bounded resume even when the generic resume flag is off. It runs the same fa `--session` (the session is still on the runner) after a backoff (default 90s, `customParams.providerTransientBackoffSec`). At most one resume per leg.
3. If the resume fails, the existing reset path runs, but the comment says `⏸️ Provider outage (<model list>, <codes>) — reset for retry`. It does not blame a rate limit when the cause was a 500.
4. The run conclusion stays failure (gh-742 contract) on reset, and success if the resume lands `response.md`.

Invariants:
- I1 — quota_exhausted keeps priority (gh-1087 park).
- I2 — never more than one resume per leg.
- I3 — fatal environment errors still throw.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — the log fixture from run 39315836954 classifies as `provider_transient` (UT-1).
- **AC2** — a 403/quota fixture still yields `quota_exhausted` (REG-1).
- **AC3** — with `provider_transient`, resume is attempted once even when resume is disabled globally (UT-2, mock feedbackLoop).
- **AC4** — resume lands response.md → normal PR path, no reset (UT-3).
- **AC5** — resume fails → reset, and the comment names the provider + codes (UT-4).
- **AC6** — the backoff is configurable and honored (UT-5, fake timer/sleep injection).

## Non-goals
Changing the provider queue composition; adding providers.

## References
Run 39315836954; gh-742, gh-1087, gh-1045; js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js `recoverMissingResponse`.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

#!/bin/bash
# Fa provider for run-agent.sh
#
# fa headless contract (env preconfig — the declaration is machine-written
# and self-contained; fa never guesses catalog defaults):
#   FA_PROVIDER_TYPE     (required) catalog provider kind: anthropic,
#                        google, dial, openai-completions, zai, aiin,
#                        minimax, chatgpt-codex, copilot, codemie,
#                        ollama, openai, openrouter, kimi, …
#   FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG   (required, JSON) {"baseUrl": …, "model": …,
#                        "apiKeyEnvVar": …} — baseUrl and model are
#                        mandatory (fa fails the boot without them),
#                        apiKeyEnvVar names the env var that carries the
#                        API key (its _BASE64 twin also accepted)
#   FA_PROVIDER_NAME     (optional) unique entry name override
#   FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY  (optional) convenience: mapped into the env var
#                        the config's apiKeyEnvVar names — ONLY inside
#                        the fa subprocess scope
#
# Sessions (when agents/setup/fa-session.sh is present, e.g. AI Teammate
# runs): --session "$FA_SESSION_NAME" --session-root "$FA_SESSION_ROOT"
# resume-or-create the deterministic named session for repo:ticket:group.

_fa_resolve_env() {
  if [ -z "${FA_PROVIDER_TYPE:-}" ]; then
    echo "Error: FA_PROVIDER_TYPE environment variable is required for fa provider" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  if [ -z "${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG:-}" ]; then
    echo "Error: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is required for fa provider — a JSON object with at least {\"baseUrl\", \"model\"} (fa never guesses catalog defaults), e.g." >&2
    echo "  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{\"baseUrl\":\"https://ai-proxy.lab.epam.com\",\"model\":\"gpt-4o\",\"apiKeyEnvVar\":\"DIAL_API_KEY\"}'" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  # Surface the config's key env var name so the runner can map
  # FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY into it for the subprocess when the var itself
  # is unset.
  FA_KEY_ENV_VAR="$(printf '%s' "${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG}" | sed -n 's/.*"apiKeyEnvVar"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
}

run_fa() {
  _fa_resolve_env || return 1

  _fa_configure_session

  echo "Fa Configuration:"
  echo "  Provider Type: ${FA_PROVIDER_TYPE}"
  [ -n "${FA_PROVIDER_NAME:-}" ] && echo "  Entry Name: ${FA_PROVIDER_NAME}"
  echo "  Config: ${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG}"

  local pass_args=()
  local arg
  for arg in ${PASS_ARGS[@]+"${PASS_ARGS[@]}"}; do
    case "$arg" in
      --continue|--resume) ;;
      *) pass_args+=("$arg") ;;
    esac
  done

  # Provider selection is driven entirely by the FA_PROVIDER_* env
  # preconfig (fa precedence: explicit flags > preconfig > saved config).
  # No --provider/--model/--base-url flags here — the env declaration is
  # the single source of truth and pins every model role.
  local cmd
  cmd=(fa)
  if [ -n "${FA_SESSION_NAME:-}" ] && [ -n "${FA_SESSION_ROOT:-}" ]; then
    cmd+=(--session "${FA_SESSION_NAME}" --session-root "${FA_SESSION_ROOT}")
  fi
  # FA_LOG_FILE (optional): tee fa's full stdout trace (assistant text, tool
  # calls) to this file — untruncated, unlike the terminal-width trajectory
  # rows. CI tails/uploads it; requires fa >= v0.1.335 (--log-file).
  # Callers can still pass --log-file explicitly via PASS_ARGS.
  if [ -n "${FA_LOG_FILE:-}" ] \
    && ! printf '%s\n' ${pass_args[@]+"${pass_args[@]}"} | grep -qx -- '--log-file'; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "${FA_LOG_FILE}")"
    cmd+=(--log-file "${FA_LOG_FILE}")
  fi
  cmd+=(${pass_args[@]+"${pass_args[@]}"} -p "$PROMPT")

  echo "Working directory: $(pwd)"
  echo ""
  echo "Running: ${cmd[*]}"
  echo ""

  local agent_log
  agent_log="$(mktemp)"

  # Map FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY into the env var the config's apiKeyEnvVar
  # names — ONLY for the fa subprocess (claude.sh maps CLAUDE_CODE_* →
  # ANTHROPIC_* the same way) so it never leaks into the surrounding job
  # environment. When the caller already exported the named var, fa reads
  # it directly and nothing is injected.
  set +e
  if [ -n "${FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY:-}" ] && [ -n "${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR:-}" ] \
     && [ -z "$(eval "echo \${${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR}:-}")" ]; then
    env "${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR}=${FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY}" "${cmd[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$agent_log"
  else
    "${cmd[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$agent_log"
  fi
  local exit_code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
  set -e

  record_codegraph_usage "$agent_log"
  rm -f "$agent_log"

  echo ""
  echo "=== Agent completed with exit code: $exit_code ==="
  return $exit_code
}

# Configure the deterministic session when the setup script is available
# (repo-local runs may not have it — fa then runs without a named session).
# Runs inside run_fa's caller context, NOT at source time: sourcing here
# would otherwise run before the provider env validation and leak setup
# vars into unrelated shells.
_fa_configure_session() {
  local setup_dir
  setup_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../setup" 2>/dev/null && pwd || true)"
  if [ -z "${FA_SESSION_NAME:-}" ] && [ -f "${setup_dir}/fa-session.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source "${setup_dir}/fa-session.sh" env
  fi
}

So a plain re-invocation of `run-agent.sh` with the fa provider already resumes the persisted session (resume-or-create). That means the "bounded resume" mechanism (feedbackLoop.resumeAgent with `--continue`) works for the fa provider as "resume the same session".

# gh-1121: Dev leg: provider-chain outage (5xx/429) → resume persisted fa session once instead of cold reset; honest cause in comment

## Description

## Goal — a provider outage mid-leg resumes the same session instead of a cold reset (v1)
One sentence: **when the fa CLI exits because the whole provider chain failed with transient errors (5xx / 429), the dev leg is classified `provider_transient`, resumes the persisted fa session once after a backoff, and falls back to the cold reset only if the resume also fails. The ticket comment names the real cause.**

## Live evidence
- Run IstiN/dmtools-agents#39315836954 (job 118277233621), gh-1112, 2026-10-19 20:02–20:14.
- `zai/glm-5.3-flash` returned 500 `{"code":"1234","message":"Internal network failure"}` ×3. `kimi-for-coding` then hit `429 Rate limit reached` ×12, giving `Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2 chain model(s) failed after 6 attempt(s) over 330s`. The agent exited with code 1 after 11 requests and 97k prompt tokens of real work. The session was persisted to `fa-sess/gh-1112`.
- `recoverMissingResponse`:
  - `quotaParkGate`: no (not a quota error, correct).
  - `isFatalCliEnvironmentError`: no.
  - `resumeOnceForMissingResponse` → `Bounded resume … not attempted (disabled)`.
  - Result: cold reset to Ready For Development, a comment saying "likely hit a rate limit", and a red run.
- All of the work is discarded, and the next leg starts from scratch, likely into the same outage.

## Architecture
1. `classifyInterruptedText` / `quotaBreaker.classifyFailure` gains the kind `provider_transient`: matches `Provider chain exhausted` together with only 5xx / 429 / network attempts (no 401/403/quota text).
2. For `provider_transient`, `recoverMissingResponse` performs the bounded resume even when the generic resume flag is off. It runs the same fa `--session` (the session is still on the runner) after a backoff (default 90s, `customParams.providerTransientBackoffSec`). At most one resume per leg.
3. If the resume fails, the existing reset path runs, but the comment says `⏸️ Provider outage (<model list>, <codes>) — reset for retry`. It does not blame a rate limit when the cause was a 500.
4. The run conclusion stays failure (gh-742 contract) on reset, and success if the resume lands `response.md`.

Invariants:
- I1 — quota_exhausted keeps priority (gh-1087 park).
- I2 — never more than one resume per leg.
- I3 — fatal environment errors still throw.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — the log fixture from run 39315836954 classifies as `provider_transient` (UT-1).
- **AC2** — a 403/quota fixture still yields `quota_exhausted` (REG-1).
- **AC3** — with `provider_transient`, resume is attempted once even when resume is disabled globally (UT-2, mock feedbackLoop).
- **AC4** — resume lands response.md → normal PR path, no reset (UT-3).
- **AC5** — resume fails → reset, and the comment names the provider + codes (UT-4).
- **AC6** — the backoff is configurable and honored (UT-5, fake timer/sleep injection).

## Non-goals
Changing the provider queue composition; adding providers.

## References
Run 39315836954; gh-742, gh-1087, gh-1045; js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js `recoverMissingResponse`.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

#!/bin/bash
# Fa provider for run-agent.sh
#
# fa headless contract (env preconfig — the declaration is machine-written
# and self-contained; fa never guesses catalog defaults):
#   FA_PROVIDER_TYPE     (required) catalog provider kind: anthropic,
#                        google, dial, openai-completions, zai, aiin,
#                        minimax, chatgpt-codex, copilot, codemie,
#                        ollama, openai, openrouter, kimi, …
#   FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG   (required, JSON) {"baseUrl": …, "model": …,
#                        "apiKeyEnvVar": …} — baseUrl and model are
#                        mandatory (fa fails the boot without them),
#                        apiKeyEnvVar names the env var that carries the
#                        API key (its _BASE64 twin also accepted)
#   FA_PROVIDER_NAME     (optional) unique entry name override
#   FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY  (optional) convenience: mapped into the env var
#                        the config's apiKeyEnvVar names — ONLY inside
#                        the fa subprocess scope
#
# Sessions (when agents/setup/fa-session.sh is present, e.g. AI Teammate
# runs): --session "$FA_SESSION_NAME" --session-root "$FA_SESSION_ROOT"
# resume-or-create the deterministic named session for repo:ticket:group.

_fa_resolve_env() {
  if [ -z "${FA_PROVIDER_TYPE:-}" ]; then
    echo "Error: FA_PROVIDER_TYPE environment variable is required for fa provider" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  if [ -z "${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG:-}" ]; then
    echo "Error: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is required for fa provider — a JSON object with at least {\"baseUrl\", \"model\"} (fa never guesses catalog defaults), e.g." >&2
    echo "  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{\"baseUrl\":\"https://ai-proxy.lab.epam.com\",\"model\":\"gpt-4o\",\"apiKeyEnvVar\":\"DIAL_API_KEY\"}'" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  # Surface the config's key env var name so the runner can map
  # FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY into it for the subprocess when the var itself
  # is unset.
  FA_KEY_ENV_VAR="$(printf '%s' "${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG}" | sed -n 's/.*"apiKeyEnvVar"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
}

run_fa() {
  _fa_resolve_env || return 1

  _fa_configure_session

  echo "Fa Configuration:"
  echo "  Provider Type: ${FA_PROVIDER_TYPE}"
  [ -n "${FA_PROVIDER_NAME:-}" ] && echo "  Entry Name: ${FA_PROVIDER_NAME}"
  echo "  Config: ${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG}"

  local pass_args=()
  local arg
  for arg in ${PASS_ARGS[@]+"${PASS_ARGS[@]}"}; do
    case "$arg" in
      --continue|--resume) ;;
      *) pass_args+=("$arg") ;;
    esac
  done

  # Provider selection is driven entirely by the FA_PROVIDER_* env
  # preconfig (fa precedence: explicit flags > preconfig > saved config).
  # No --provider/--model/--base-url flags here — the env declaration is
  # the single source of truth and pins every model role.
  local cmd
  cmd=(fa)
  if [ -n "${FA_SESSION_NAME:-}" ] && [ -n "${FA_SESSION_ROOT:-}" ]; then
    cmd+=(--session "${FA_SESSION_NAME}" --session-root "${FA_SESSION_ROOT}")
  fi
  # FA_LOG_FILE (optional): tee fa's full stdout trace (assistant text, tool
  # calls) to this file — untruncated, unlike the terminal-width trajectory
  # rows. CI tails/uploads it; requires fa >= v0.1.335 (--log-file).
  # Callers can still pass --log-file explicitly via PASS_ARGS.
  if [ -n "${FA_LOG_FILE:-}" ] \
    && ! printf '%s\n' ${pass_args[@]+"${pass_args[@]}"} | grep -qx -- '--log-file'; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "${FA_LOG_FILE}")"
    cmd+=(--log-file "${FA_LOG_FILE}")
  fi
  cmd+=(${pass_args[@]+"${pass_args[@]}"} -p "$PROMPT")

  echo "Working directory: $(pwd)"
  echo ""
  echo "Running: ${cmd[*]}"
  echo ""

  local agent_log
  agent_log="$(mktemp)"

  # Map FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY into the env var the config's apiKeyEnvVar
  # names — ONLY for the fa subprocess (claude.sh maps CLAUDE_CODE_* →
  # ANTHROPIC_* the same way) so it never leaks into the surrounding job
  # environment. When the caller already exported the named var, fa reads
  # it directly and nothing is injected.
  set +e
  if [ -n "${FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY:-}" ] && [ -n "${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR:-}" ] \
     && [ -z "$(eval "echo \${${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR}:-}")" ]; then
    env "${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR}=${FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY}" "${cmd[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$agent_log"
  else
    "${cmd[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$agent_log"
  fi
  local exit_code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
  set -e

  record_codegraph_usage "$agent_log"
  rm -f "$agent_log"

  echo ""
  echo "=== Agent completed with exit code: $exit_code ==="
  return $exit_code
}

# Configure the deterministic session when the setup script is available
# (repo-local runs may not have it — fa then runs without a named session).
# Runs inside run_fa's caller context, NOT at source time: sourcing here
# would otherwise run before the provider env validation and leak setup
# vars into unrelated shells.
_fa_configure_session() {
  local setup_dir
  setup_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../setup" 2>/dev/null && pwd || true)"
  if [ -z "${FA_SESSION_NAME:-}" ] && [ -f "${setup_dir}/fa-session.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source "${setup_dir}/fa-session.sh" env
  fi
}

So the fa provider is invoked via `bash agents/scripts/run-agent.sh --continue <promptPath>`. Note that `run_fa` ignores `--continue|--resume` in PASS_ARGS but `FA_SESSION_NAME`/`FA_SESSION_ROOT` make it use `--session "$FA_SESSION_NAME" --session-root "$FA_SESSION_ROOT"` which is a "resume-or-create the deterministic named session". So a plain re-invocation of `run-agent.sh` with the fa provider already resumes the persisted session (resume-or-create). That means the "bounded resume" mechanism (feedbackLoop.resumeAgent with `--continue`) works for the fa provider as "resume the same session".

The ticket says: "It runs the same fa `--session` (the session is still on the runner) after a backoff (default 90s, `customParams.providerTransientBackoffSec`). At most one resume per leg."

So the implementation plan:

1. **quotaCircuitBreaker.classifyFailure** gains kind `provider_transient`:

The resume itself is executed by feedbackLoop.resumeAgent via cli_execute_command. The sleep injection: simplest is a `sleepBackoff(seconds)` function in feedbackLoop (or developTicketAndCreatePR) that runs `sleep <n>` via runCommand — in tests we mock `cli_execute_command`. Testable design: a pure helper `providerTransientBackoffSeconds(customParams)` returning parsed seconds (default 90), and the actual sleep via an injectable function. In feedbackLoop.js, `runCommand` is module-level using cli_execute_command global — tests already mock cli_execute_command (test_feedbackLoop mocks it). Let me check test_feedbackLoop for how they mock sleep-ish behavior.

3. **Reset comment honesty** (AC5): when the leg is reset after a provider-outage (5xx), the comment must say `⏸️ Provider outage (<model list>, <codes>) — reset for retry` rather than "likely hit a rate limit". Currently `interruptedNoChangesComment` says "likely hit a rate limit". Need a classification-aware comment: if the classification is provider_transient with providers/codes, use the honest wording. # gh-1121: Dev leg: provider-chain outage (5xx/429) → resume persisted fa session once instead of cold reset; honest cause in comment

## Description

## Goal — a provider outage mid-leg resumes the same session instead of a cold reset (v1)
One sentence: **when the fa CLI exits because the whole provider chain failed with transient errors (5xx / 429), the dev leg is classified `provider_transient`, resumes the persisted fa session once after a backoff, and falls back to the cold reset only if the resume also fails. The ticket comment names the real cause.**

## Live evidence
- Run IstiN/dmtools-agents#39315836954 (job 118277233621), gh-1112, 2026-10-19 20:02–20:14.
- `zai/glm-5.3-flash` returned 500 `{"code":"1234","message":"Internal network failure"}` ×3. `kimi-for-coding` then hit `429 Rate limit reached` ×12, giving `Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2 chain model(s) failed after 6 attempt(s) over 330s`. The agent exited with code 1 after 11 requests and 97k prompt tokens of real work. The session was persisted to `fa-sess/gh-1112`.
- `recoverMissingResponse`:
  - `quotaParkGate`: no (not a quota error, correct).
  - `isFatalCliEnvironmentError`: no.
  - `resumeOnceForMissingResponse` → `Bounded resume … not attempted (disabled)`.
  - Result: cold reset to Ready For Development, a comment saying "likely hit a rate limit", and a red run.
- All of the work is discarded, and the next leg starts from scratch, likely into the same outage.

## Architecture
1. `classifyInterruptedText` / `quotaBreaker.classifyFailure` gains the kind `provider_transient`: matches `Provider chain exhausted` together with only 5xx / 429 / network attempts (no 401/403/quota text).
2. For `provider_transient`, `recoverMissingResponse` performs the bounded resume even when the generic resume flag is off. It runs the same fa `--session` (the session is still on the runner) after a backoff (default 90s, `customParams.providerTransientBackoffSec`). At most one resume per leg.
3. If the resume fails, the existing reset path runs, but the comment says `⏸️ Provider outage (<model list>, <codes>) — reset for retry`. It does not blame a rate limit when the cause was a 500.
4. The run conclusion stays failure (gh-742 contract) on reset, and success if the resume lands `response.md`.

Invariants:
- I1 — quota_exhausted keeps priority (gh-1087 park).
- I2 — never more than one resume per leg.
- I3 — fatal environment errors still throw.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — the log fixture from run 39315836954 classifies as `provider_transient` (UT-1).
- **AC2** — a 403/quota fixture still yields `quota_exhausted` (REG-1).
- **AC3** — with `provider_transient`, resume is attempted once even when resume is disabled globally (UT-2, mock feedbackLoop).
- **AC4** — resume lands response.md → normal PR path, no reset (UT-3).
- **AC5** — resume fails → reset, and the comment names the provider + codes (UT-4).
- **AC6** — the backoff is configurable and honored (UT-5, fake timer/sleep injection).

## Non-goals
Changing the provider queue composition; adding providers.

## References
Run 39315836954; gh-742, gh-1087, gh-1045; js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js `recoverMissingResponse`.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`
  afterwards, and `--alwaysPostComments false` to keep the test ticket quiet.
- After the run, verify the side effects directly (e.g. `jira_get_ticket`,
  `confluence_content_by_id`, `confluence_get_page_inline_comments`) rather
  than trusting the job log.

## Conventions

### No project-specific content — STRICT RULE

**This is a public, product-agnostic repository. NEVER commit anything company- or customer-specific here.** Violations are a fireable offense and require history rewrite.

Forbidden anywhere in this repo (code, comments, prompts, instructions, tests, docs, commit messages):

- Company, customer, or product names
- Internal hostnames, URLs, IPs, Jira/Confluence links, real ticket keys
- Internal label/branch/repo naming conventions tied to one organization
- File paths pointing to internal repos, internal registry URLs
- Sample data copied from real internal systems

Everything here must be **generic and configurable**: names like `example.com`, `PROJ-123`, `acme`; behavior driven by `customParams` / `.dmtools/config.js` in the consuming repo. Project context goes in the target repo's `.dmtools/config.js` or the corporate orchestrator repo…

#!/bin/bash
# Fa provider for run-agent.sh
#
# fa headless contract (env preconfig — the declaration is machine-written
# and self-contained; fa never guesses catalog defaults):
#   FA_PROVIDER_TYPE     (required) catalog provider kind: anthropic,
#                        google, dial, openai-completions, zai, aiin,
#                        minimax, chatgpt-codex, copilot, codemie,
#                        ollama, openai, openrouter, kimi, …
#   FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG   (required, JSON) {"baseUrl": …, "model": …,
#                        "apiKeyEnvVar": …} — baseUrl and model are
#                        mandatory (fa fails the boot without them),
#                        apiKeyEnvVar names the env var that carries the
#                        API key (its _BASE64 twin also accepted)
#   FA_PROVIDER_NAME     (optional) unique entry name override
#   FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY  (optional) convenience: mapped into the env var
#                        the config's apiKeyEnvVar names — ONLY inside
#                        the fa subprocess scope
#
# Sessions (when agents/setup/fa-session.sh is present, e.g. AI Teammate
# runs): --session "$FA_SESSION_NAME" --session-root "$FA_SESSION_ROOT"
# resume-or-create the deterministic named session for repo:ticket:group.

_fa_resolve_env() {
  if [ -z "${FA_PROVIDER_TYPE:-}" ]; then
    echo "Error: FA_PROVIDER_TYPE environment variable is required for fa provider" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  if [ -z "${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG:-}" ]; then
    echo "Error: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is required for fa provider — a JSON object with at least {\"baseUrl\", \"model\"} (fa never guesses catalog defaults), e.g." >&2
    echo "  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{\"baseUrl\":\"https://ai-proxy.lab.epam.com\",\"model\":\"gpt-4o\",\"apiKeyEnvVar\":\"DIAL_API_KEY\"}'" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  # Surface the config's key env var name so the runner can map
  # FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY into it for the subprocess when the var itself
  # is unset.
  FA_KEY_ENV_VAR="$(printf '%s' "${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG}" | sed -n 's/.*"apiKeyEnvVar"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
}

run_fa() {
  _fa_resolve_env || return 1

  _fa_configure_session

  echo "Fa Configuration:"
  echo "  Provider Type: ${FA_PROVIDER_TYPE}"
  [ -n "${FA_PROVIDER_NAME:-}" ] && echo "  Entry Name: ${FA_PROVIDER_NAME}"
  echo "  Config: ${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG}"

  local pass_args=()
  local arg
  for arg in ${PASS_ARGS[@]+"${PASS_ARGS[@]}"}; do
    case "$arg" in
      --continue|--resume) ;;
      *) pass_args+=("$arg") ;;
    esac
  done

  # Provider selection is driven entirely by the FA_PROVIDER_* env
  # preconfig (fa precedence: explicit flags > preconfig > saved config).
  # No --provider/--model/--base-url flags here — the env declaration is
  # the single source of truth and pins every model role.
  local cmd
  cmd=(fa)
  if [ -n "${FA_SESSION_NAME:-}" ] && [ -n "${FA_SESSION_ROOT:-}" ]; then
    cmd+=(--session "${FA_SESSION_NAME}" --session-root "${FA_SESSION_ROOT}")
  fi
  # FA_LOG_FILE (optional): tee fa's full stdout trace (assistant text, tool
  # calls) to this file — untruncated, unlike the terminal-width trajectory
  # rows. CI tails/uploads it; requires fa >= v0.1.335 (--log-file).
  # Callers can still pass --log-file explicitly via PASS_ARGS.
  if [ -n "${FA_LOG_FILE:-}" ] \
    && ! printf '%s\n' ${pass_args[@]+"${pass_args[@]}"} | grep -qx -- '--log-file'; then
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "${FA_LOG_FILE}")"
    cmd+=(--log-file "${FA_LOG_FILE}")
  fi
  cmd+=(${pass_args[@]+"${pass_args[@]}"} -p "$PROMPT")

  echo "Working directory: $(pwd)"
  echo ""
  echo "Running: ${cmd[*]}"
  echo ""

  local agent_log
  agent_log="$(mktemp)"

  # Map FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY into the env var the config's apiKeyEnvVar
  # names — ONLY for the fa subprocess (claude.sh maps CLAUDE_CODE_* →
  # ANTHROPIC_* the same way) so it never leaks into the surrounding job
  # environment. When the caller already exported the named var, fa reads
  # it directly and nothing is injected.
  set +e
  if [ -n "${FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY:-}" ] && [ -n "${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR:-}" ] \
     && [ -z "$(eval "echo \${${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR}:-}")" ]; then
    env "${FA_KEY_ENV_VAR}=${FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY}" "${cmd[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$agent_log"
  else
    "${cmd[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$agent_log"
  fi
  local exit_code=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
  set -e

  record_codegraph_usage "$agent_log"
  rm -f "$agent_log"

  echo ""
  echo "=== Agent completed with exit code: $exit_code ==="
  return $exit_code
}

# Configure the deterministic session when the setup script is available
# (repo-local runs may not have it — fa then runs without a named session).
# Runs inside run_fa's caller context, NOT at source time: sourcing here
# would otherwise run before the provider env validation and leak setup
# vars into unrelated shells.
_fa_configure_session() {
  local setup_dir
  setup_dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../../setup" 2>/dev/null && pwd || true)"
  if [ -z "${FA_SESSION_NAME:-}" ] && [ -f "${setup_dir}/fa-session.sh" ]; then
    # shellcheck source=/dev/null
    source "${setup_dir}/fa-session.sh" env
  fi
}

So the fa provider is invoked via `bash agents/scripts/run-agent.sh --continue <promptPath>`. Note that `run_fa` ignores `--continue|--resume` in PASS_ARGS but `FA_SESSION_NAME`/`FA_SESSION_ROOT` make it use `--session "$FA_SESSION_NAME" --session-root "$FA_SESSION_ROOT"` which is a "resume-or-create the deterministic named session". So a plain re-invocation of `run-agent.sh` with the fa provider already resumes the persisted session (resume-or-create). That means the "bounded resume" mechanism (feedbackLoop.resumeAgent with `--continue`) works for the fa provider as "resume the same session".

The ticket says: "It runs the same fa `--session` (the session is still on the runner) after a backoff (default 90s, `customParams.providerTransientBackoffSec`). At most one resume per leg."

The resume itself is executed by feedbackLoop.resumeAgent via cli_execute_command. The sleep injection: simplest is a `sleepBackoff(seconds)` function in feedbackLoop (or developTicketAndCreatePR) that runs `sleep <n>` via runCommand — in tests we mock `cli_execute_command`. Testable design: a pure helper `providerTransientBackoffSeconds(customParams)` returning parsed seconds (default 90), and the actual sleep via an injectable function. In feedbackLoop.js, `runCommand` is module-level using cli_execute_command global — tests already mock cli_execute_command (test_feedbackLoop mocks it). Let me check test_feedbackLoop for how they mock sleep-ish behavior.

Currently `interruptedNoChangesComment` says "likely hit a rate limit". Need a classification-aware comment: if the classification is provider_transient with providers/codes, use the honest wording. "only 5xx/429/network attempts" — a bare chain-exhausted text has no attempt evidence at all. Strictly "only 5xx/429/network" with zero attempts... ambiguous. I'd say: bare chain-exhausted without any evidence → treat as provider_transient? Or null?

# gh-1121: Dev leg: provider-chain outage (5xx/429) → resume persisted fa session once instead of cold reset; honest cause in comment

## Description

## Goal — a provider outage mid-leg resumes the same session instead of a cold reset (v1)
One sentence: **when the fa CLI exits because the whole provider chain failed with transient errors (5xx / 429), the dev leg is classified `provider_transient`, resumes the persisted fa session once after a backoff, and falls back to the cold reset only if the resume also fails. The ticket comment names the real cause.**

## Live evidence
- Run IstiN/dmtools-agents#39315836954 (job 118277233621), gh-1112, 2026-10-19 20:02–20:14.
- `zai/glm-5.3-flash` returned 500 `{"code":"1234","message":"Internal network failure"}` ×3. `kimi-for-coding` then hit `429 Rate limit reached` ×12, giving `Provider chain exhausted: 2 of 2 chain model(s) failed after 6 attempt(s) over 330s`. The agent exited with code 1 after 11 requests and 97k prompt tokens of real work. The session was persisted to `fa-sess/gh-1112`.
- `recoverMissingResponse`:
  - `quotaParkGate`: no (not a quota error, correct).
  - `isFatalCliEnvironmentError`: no.
  - `resumeOnceForMissingResponse` → `Bounded resume … not attempted (disabled)`.
  - Result: cold reset to Ready For Development, a comment saying "likely hit a rate limit", and a red run.
- All of the work is discarded, and the next leg starts from scratch, likely into the same outage.

## Architecture
1. `classifyInterruptedText` / `quotaBreaker.classifyFailure` gains the kind `provider_transient`: matches `Provider chain exhausted` together with only 5xx / 429 / network attempts (no 401/403/quota text).
2. For `provider_transient`, `recoverMissingResponse` performs the bounded resume even when the generic resume flag is off. It runs the same fa `--session` (the session is still on the runner) after a backoff (default 90s, `customParams.providerTransientBackoffSec`). At most one resume per leg.
3. If the resume fails, the existing reset path runs, but the comment says `⏸️ Provider outage (<model list>, <codes>) — reset for retry`. It does not blame a rate limit when the cause was a 500.
4. The run conclusion stays failure (gh-742 contract) on reset, and success if the resume lands `response.md`.

Invariants:
- I1 — quota_exhausted keeps priority (gh-1087 park).
- I2 — never more than one resume per leg.
- I3 — fatal environment errors still throw.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — the log fixture from run 39315836954 classifies as `provider_transient` (UT-1).
- **AC2** — a 403/quota fixture still yields `quota_exhausted` (REG-1).
- **AC3** — with `provider_transient`, resume is attempted once even when resume is disabled globally (UT-2, mock feedbackLoop).
- **AC4** — resume lands response.md → normal PR path, no reset (UT-3).
- **AC5** — resume fails → reset, and the comment names the provider + codes (UT-4).
- **AC6** — the backoff is configurable and honored (UT-5, fake timer/sleep injection).

## Non-goals
Changing the provider queue composition; adding providers.

## References
Run 39315836954; gh-742, gh-1087, gh-1045; js/developTicketAndCreatePR.js `recoverMissingResponse`.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- **Requires resolve by execution time** (gh-823): a require that runs while a module initializes (top level, top-level `try`/`if`) resolves **file-relative**; a require that runs **after init** (any lazy/deferred call into an exported function) resolves against the **main script's directory — the pack's `js/` root — exclusively**, and a file-relative hit is never tried. `dmtools compile` discovers the pack closure strictly file-relative. Therefore: **hoist every require to the top of the module — never require lazily.** A lazy sibling-flat spec from `js/common/` looks for `js/x.js` and reds the tick ("Failed to require module"), and a pack-root-relative spec (`./common/…`) authored from a nested file fails the pack build. (Worker-source strings are the one exception — they execute on fresh engines and are authored js-root-relative: `require('./common/smProvider.js')`.) The repo-wide pin in `js/unit-tests/test_packRequirePath.js` fails the suite on ANY deferred require in packed code; its `ALLOWED_DEFERRED` list carries exactly one deliberate entry — `writeSolutionAndDiagrams.js`'s cycle-breaking `require('./writeSolutionAndLabels.js')` (hoisting it would close the labels→diagrams cycle at load time) — don't add a second one.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

- Create or extend a `js/unit-tests/test_<module>.js` file.
- Add it to the corresponding `run_<module>.json` (or create a new one) and include it in `run_all.json`.
- Use `loadModule('js/your-module.js', makeRequire({...}), { globalMock: fn })` to isolate the module.
- Mock all dmtools globals (`file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`, `jira_*`, `github_*`, etc.) — never let tests call real services.
- Block config file discovery in mocks: return `null` for any path containing `.dmtools/config` to prevent loading a parent repo's real config.
- Project-specific test suites (loading files from `.dmtools/`) must guard with a file-existence check so they skip gracefully in standalone context.

Example mock pattern:
```js
var fileReadMock = function(opts) {
    var p = opts && (opts.path || opts);
    if (fileMap[p] !== undefined) return fileMap[p];
    if (p && p.indexOf('.dmtools/config') !== -1) return null; // block real config
    try { return file_read(opts); } catch (e) { return null; }
};
```

### Live end-to-end testing without an AI CLI

Unit tests cover JS logic with mocks, but a Teammate agent's full wiring
(preJSAction → input context → preCliJSAction → CLI → postJSAction) can also
be exercised against **real Jira/Confluence/etc.** without invoking the real
AI CLI (`scripts/run-agent.sh`). Two dmtools features make this possible:

1. **CLI param overrides** — `dmtools run <config.json> --key value` patches
   the `params` block. Values that look like JSON arrays/objects are parsed as
   JSON, so even `cliCommands` and `customParams` can be overridden:

   ```bash
   dmtools run agents/story_solution.json \
     --inputJql "key = PROJ-123" \
     --cliCommands '["/path/to/fake_cli.sh"]' \
     --customParams '{"contentOutput":{"target":"confluence","space":"DOC","parentPageId":"123456"}}' \
     --alwaysPostComments false \
     --cleanupInputFolder false
   ```

2. **A fake CLI script** that mimics the agent contract: read `input/`, write
   `outputs/response.md` (and any other files the post-action expects, e.g.
   `outputs/confluence_replies.json`). Keep it outside the repo (it is
   project- and machine-specific):

   ```bash
   #!/bin/bash
   set -e
   mkdir -p outputs
   printf '# Fake output\n\nGenerated by the e2e fake CLI.\n' > outputs/response.md
   ```

Rules for live e2e runs:

- **Never commit live-e2e configs or scripts to this repo** — they contain
  real ticket keys, page IDs and space keys, which violates the
  project-agnostic rule. Keep them in a scratch directory or pass everything
  via CLI overrides.
- Run against **dedicated garbage objects** (a test ticket and a test
  Confluence page clearly marked "safe to delete"), never real work items.
- Pass `--cleanupInputFolder false` so you can inspect `input/<KEY>/`

#!/bin/bash
# Fa provider for run-agent.sh
#
# fa headless contract (env preconfig — the declaration is machine-written
# and self-contained; fa never guesses catalog defaults):
#   FA_PROVIDER_TYPE     (required) catalog provider kind: anthropic,
#                        google, dial, openai-completions, zai, aiin,
#                        minimax, chatgpt-codex, copilot, codemie,
#                        ollama, openai, openrouter, kimi, …
#   FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG   (required, JSON) {"baseUrl": …, "model": …,
#                        "apiKeyEnvVar": …} — baseUrl and model are
#                        mandatory (fa fails the boot without them),
#                        apiKeyEnvVar names the env var that carries the
#                        API key (its _BASE64 twin also accepted)
#   FA_PROVIDER_NAME     (optional) unique entry name override
#   FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY  (optional) convenience: mapped into the env var
#                        the config's apiKeyEnvVar names — ONLY inside
#                        the fa subprocess scope
#
# Sessions (when agents/setup/fa-session.sh is present, e.g. AI Teammate
# runs): --session "$FA_SESSION_NAME" --session-root "$FA_SESSION_ROOT"
# resume-or-create the deterministic named session for repo:ticket:group.

_fa_resolve_env() {
  if [ -z "${FA_PROVIDER_TYPE:-}" ]; then
    echo "Error: FA_PROVIDER_TYPE environment variable is required for fa provider" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  if [ -z "${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG:-}" ]; then
    echo "Error: FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG is required for fa provider — a JSON object with at least {\"baseUrl\", \"model\"} (fa never guesses catalog defaults), e.g." >&2
    echo "  FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG='{\"baseUrl\":\"https://ai-proxy.lab.epam.com\",\"model\":\"gpt-4o\",\"apiKeyEnvVar\":\"DIAL_API_KEY\"}'" >&2
    return 1
  fi

  # Surface the config's key env var name so the runner can map
  # FA_PROVIDER_API_KEY into it for the subprocess when the var itself
  # is unset.
  FA_KEY_ENV_VAR="$(printf '%s' "${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG}" | sed -n 's/.*"apiKeyEnvVar"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
}

run_fa() {
  _fa_resolve_env || return 1

  _fa_configure_session

  echo "Fa Configuration:"
  echo "  Provider Type: ${FA_PROVIDER_TYPE}"
  [ -n "${FA_PROVIDER_NAME:-}" ] && echo "  Entry Name: ${FA_PROVIDER_NAME}"
  echo "  Config: ${FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG}"

  local pass_args=()
  local arg
  for arg in ${PASS_ARGS[@]+"${PASS_ARGS[@]}"}; do
    case "$arg" in
      --continue|--resume) ;;
      *) pass_args+=("$arg") ;;
    esac
  done

  # preconfig (fa precedence: explicit flags > preconfig > saved config).

  local cmd
